text:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache slab pressure crossing threshold in us-west2. Streaming generation p95 and p99 spiking. Error budget burn 3.7% in the last 5m. Auto-escalating to #eng-oncall.

maria: seeing it on dashboards — p95 gen latency jumped from ~420ms -> 980ms, p99 up to ~3.1s. Streaming stalls: many connections showing stalled chunks >1s.

ash: confirmed. KV shard load uneven; some slabs approaching 95% occupancy and we’re seeing frequent evictions. Prefill queues are backed up, decode workers starved. Looks like prefill vs decode imbalance + fragmentation.

maria: impact? which customers affected? any errors returned or just latency?

lina: support reports for a few customers (acct IDs redacted) with degraded streaming (chunk timeouts) and some user-facing timeouts at 10s. No 5xx spike yet, mostly timeouts and degraded UX.

carol: product question — are any Canary apps hitting this or is this general traffic?

ash: mostly general traffic in us-west2. Canary traffic looks ok (lower qps) but background prefill burst at minute boundaries pushed the slab allocator into fragmentation.

maria: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) throttle prefill workers 2) lower prefill concurrency 3) force decode path on hot keys to avoid long-lived prefill KV entries 4) temporarily increase slab pool on affected nodes 5) start rolling restart of a subset of inference workers to free fragmented slabs. Thoughts?

jorge: agree. My priority ordering: throttle prefill -> enable immediate decode fallback -> bump slab size -> rolling restart if still bad. Rolling restart will be last resort (disruptive).

ash: adding concrete ops steps below. I'll run the throttle and toggle fallback now.

ash: ops commands:
```
# throttle prefill workers for model: rwd-1.1
kubectl -n inference patch deploy prefill-deployer --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":2}]'
# enable decode-fallback (feature flag)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/flags/decode_fallback/enable
# monitor logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference -c kvcache --tail=200 | grep -i "evict"
```

deploy-bot: Deploy rwd-1.1_prefill-throttle rolled out to us-west2 (2 replicas) — 1m ago.

maria: after throttle: p95 dropped from 980ms -> 610ms in the last 2m. p99 still ~1.9s. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated. Good sign.

lina: customers reported improvement in some sessions; one key customer still sees intermittent stalls. Escalated to account owner.

ash: next I'm going to enable immediate decode fallback (it forces decode attempt even if prefill present, reduces long-lived prefill objects). Doing that now.

ash: toggled decode_fallback=on. Watching metrics.

maria: p99 moved from 3.1s -> 2.2s, p95 ~480ms. Streaming stalls count down ~45% vs peak.

jorge: plan for medium-term: schedule slab pool resize for the hotspot hosts + increase reclaim aggressiveness to avoid fragmentation. Also consider a small change to eviction policy: prefer LRU over age-based for hot keys. Will follow up with eng-runtime.

ash: I see one host (node-uw2-13) with high fragmentation; I'll cordon and drain it for a controlled reboot if needed.

maria: customer impact note: mark incident as P2 and notify CS with current mitigations and ETA. Lina, can you draft a short note?

lina: drafted, sending to CS and the affected account owners: "We're investigating elevated latency in us-west2 for streaming. We've throttled background prefetches and enabled decode fallback; we're monitoring and will update in 30m or on significant change."

carol: product wants a post-incident writeup focusing on how prefill scheduling interacts with slab allocation — can we capture traces for a couple of requests?

ash: yes, enable request tracing for affected models for the next 15m. Command:
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/tracing" -d '{"model":"rwd-1.1","duration_s":900}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```

maria: handoff: I'm on till 03:00 UTC. If this stabilizes we'll transition to Jorge for overnight monitoring. Jorge, prep checklist: keep prefill at 2 replicas, keep decode_fallback=on, watch p95/p99 and streaming stall metric, if p99 > 2.5s for 5m -> escalate to eng-sre and consider rolling restart of affected nodes.

jorge: got it. I'll take over at 03:00 UTC. Adding runbook link here: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fragmentation.

ash: note for postmortem: consider adding hysteresis to prefill bursts (spread prefill over window) and slab defrag background job. Also test smaller slab allocations with heavy prefill in staging.

maria: ok summarizing: 1) throttle prefill -> done 2) enable decode fallback -> done 3) monitor metrics + tracing -> done 4) cordon node-uw2-13 if fragment doesn't reduce -> pending 5) customer comms -> done 6) handoff to Jorge at 03:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0452 - KV cache fragmentation / streaming stalls in us-west2. Sev: P2. Linked to this thread.

jorge: I'll keep an eye overnight and will open #incidents if we see regression. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all. Please add any additional notes into the incident doc and capture the final timeline.
